newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Official denies Angola supporting Zaire rebels.
newsitem.headline: Official denies Angola supporting Zaire rebels.

text.p: A senior Angolan official in the oil-rich Cabinda enclave on Wednesday denied backing rebels in eastern Zaire.

Cabinda governor Jose Amaro Tati told the state news agency Angop that Angolan government soldiers were too busy fighting separatist guerrillas in its own territory to be involved in neighbouring Zaire.

Cabinda, which supplies the bulk of Angola's oil export, is separated from the rest of Angola by a 25-km (15-mile) -long strip of Zairean territory on the Atlantic ocean. Flec (Front for the Liberation of Cabinda Enclave) has fought a long-standing guerrilla war against the government for independence.
It was not party to a 1994 peace agreement between the Angolan government and former rebel movement UNITA which ended a 19-year civil war.
United Nations and diplomatic sources in Luanda told Reuters on Tuesday both the government and UNITA had moved troops into Zaire over the past few weeks.
A U.N. official said UNITA had flown troops out of bases in the diamond-rich Luzamba town in the northeast and from Jamba, its former headquarters in the southern Cuando Cubango province.

The official said UNITA was helping soldiers of Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko, a close ally of UNITA leader Jonas Savimbi, to ensure its vital diamond smuggling routes from its diggings in eastern Angola are kept open.
The government, hoping to cut off UNITA supplies, was assisting Banyamulenge rebels who began a rebellion against Zairean rule last October.

UNITA used Zaire as its main base for the smuggling of arms to its bases in central Angola during the civil war. Aircraft from Zaire continue to land in UNITA-held areas carrying fuel and food supplies.
Cabinda governor Tati said no concentration of Angolan or Zairean troops in the enclave.
"There are no concentration of troops...in Cabinda to attack...Zaire.

"Angola is not hostile towards any of its neighbours," he told the agency, reacting to reports that the government was harbouring former Katangese mercenaries to prop up Laurent Kabila's rebel forces as they advance towards Zaire's third largest city Kisangani.
The Katangese are veterans of failed secessionist wars in the southern Zaire province of Shaba in the 1970s and 1980s.

Katangese troops, some regular members of the Angolan military, together with arms have been flown to the Rwandan capital Kigali and then on to the rebel-held town of Goma in eastern Zaire, diplomats said.
The U.N. Angola Verficiation Mission, which is meant to oversee the country's peace process, said Angolan troop movements did not fall with within its mandate.
